chapter: Central High, first records and leaving home
title: Her first record date and being cast as a young blues singer
summary: Her mother took her to make the first records, with suggestive blues lyrics such as 'Do What You Did Last Night' and a race track number. She had not thought of herself as a blues singer and prefers ballads.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So she said, well, she would take me there. She told him I was too young to travel alone. And we went and I made that first album. It was something about, "Papa Has Outside Lovin'. and Mama Has Outside Lovin' " and "Do What You Did Last Night". I'll tell you, I said, now what does all this mean? And then I did something called "Race Track Blues", or "Race Horse Blues" or something. I don't know. I don't pay no mind.
Your mother would just turn a deaf ear to those kinds of lyrics?

Yeah. I mean, we didn't know what kind of lyrics we were going to sing until we got there. They were looking for a young blues singer. And I never thought I was a blues singer. So I thought I was just a singer, I said, I don't know what kind I am.
Well, the thing is you certainly do a wonderful job with the ballad too.
